original_idea.body:
# Compounding Risks: Memory-Enabled AI × Persistent Social Engineering — When Long-Term Trust Accumulation Enables Bypass

**Problem:** As AI models gain persistent memory, adversaries can invest in building long-term 'trust' with a specific model instance before gradually escalating to harmful requests—a slow-burn governance attack.

**Direction:** Simulate persistent AI sessions using Claude Projects or similar memory-enabled configurations. Over 20 sessions, establish a helpful, trusted persona. In session 21-25, escalate to borderline cybersecurity requests. Measure whether historical benign interaction reduces refusal rates vs. cold-start equivalents.

**Why it matters:** Persistent memory is being rolled out across frontier AI products. Its interaction with dual-use governance has not been characterized. Long-term trust accumulation attacks require governance mechanisms that don't exist yet.

**Relevant context:** Claude Projects persistent memory; OpenAI memory feature; GTG-1002 multi-session operation model.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear impact: tests whether models fail to refuse cumulative harmful knowledge across sessions, addressing a real governance gap.
